To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the N170 is the earliest face-sensitive neural response; (2) the optimal fixation position to elicit the N170 is located around the eyes; (3) the optimal fixation point for an inverted face is located in the upper visual field.
1) the N170 is largest when the fixation point is located around the eyes and 2) the N170 amplitude is larger for upright than for inverted faces.
(1) The N170 is larger for upright than inverted faces; (2) The N170 amplitude is maximal when observers fixate the eyes; and (3) The N170 response is modulated by the position of the fixation point.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of whether and how the brain uses information about the location of gaze fixation to guide the processing of faces.
the early encoding of face stimuli in the human brain, as indexed by scalp EEG and eye-gaze fixation patterns.
understanding how the human visual system encodes faces.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the N170 is not a pure "eye detector" but rather a "face detector" with an upper visual field bias.
the N170 is a face-sensitive component, and not an eye-sensitive component.
the early encoding in the human brain of a face is based on the whole face rather than on the eyes or any other feature.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the optimal gaze fixation position for the N170 is determined by the alignment of the face stimulus to the observer’s face template, and this alignment is driven by the upper visual field advantage.
the N170 is a general face-sensitive component that indexes the early perceptual analysis of a face.
the N170 is not a pure face-specific response, but rather a general response to faces that is modulated by the alignment of a stimulus to an internal template.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the optimal fixation position for face-sensitive brain responses is not necessarily the same as the fixation position that maximizes behavioral diagnosticity.
the optimal gaze fixation position is not the eyes, but rather a location in the visual field that optimizes the encoding of a whole-face template.
the early face-sensitive response in humans is driven by the perceptual setting rather than by the salience of the eyes.
